title: Wildcard Word Dictionary
statement:
Implement a word dictionary whose lookups accept `.` as a wildcard.

Contract
- `add(word)` stores a non-empty lowercase word (letters `a` to `z`). Adding a word twice changes nothing.
- `matches(pattern)` takes a non-empty pattern of lowercase letters and `.` characters. It returns true if some stored word has the same length as the pattern and agrees with it at every position, where `.` agrees with any single letter.
- A pattern must match a whole word: `"ca"` does not match the stored word `"cat"`.

Examples
- After adding `tree`, `trap`, and `tone`: `matches("tr.e")` and `matches("t..e")` are true, `matches("t.o")` is false.
- After adding `cat`: `matches("cat")` is true, `matches("ca")` and `matches("cats")` are false.
- An empty dictionary matches nothing, not even `.`.

examples.input: add tree, trap, tone; matches tr.e, t..e, t.o
add cat; matches cat, ca, cats

hints: Store the words in a trie; a pattern without wildcards is then just a walk down the tree.
At a `.`, try every existing child and succeed if any branch matches the rest of the pattern. Remember that a pattern only matches when it ends exactly where a stored word ends.

Recurse on the pattern position and the current node. Intended complexity: for words of bounded length with n words stored, O(n) space and O(L) time per add, with a lookup visiting at most the stored letters; the workload keeps both pattern and word length fixed so total time is O(n).
inputSyntax: Input: operations separated by commas, for example: add tree, add trap, matches tr.e, matches t.o
sampleInput: add tree, add trap, matches tr.e, matches t.o
